situation: I want to ask my old manager Diane for advice on moving into product management. Haven't talked to her in 3 years.
reply: Hi Diane, I'll be upfront: I'm reaching out because I'm thinking about moving into product management and you're the first person whose advice I wanted, which feels a bit cheeky after three years. I still use your 'write the press release first' trick on every project. If you had 20 minutes in the next few weeks for a call, I'd be really grateful; if not, no hard feelings at all.
note: Name the ask honestly; a reconnect that hides a favour reads worse when the favour arrives.

situation: 大学室友，毕业后五年没怎么联系了。今天刷到她朋友圈，说在成都开了一家书店。
reply: 好久不见，一晃都五年了。刚看到你在成都开了书店，太像你会做的事了，当年宿舍里就你的书最多。店开得怎么样？不急着回，就是想跟你打个招呼。
note: 不用为断联道歉，用一个具体的原因开头，再问一个好回答的问题。

situation: Me peleé con mi amigo Diego hace un año por una tontería de dinero y no hablamos desde entonces. Quiero escribirle sin reabrir la pelea.
reply: Hola, Diego. Últimamente me he acordado mucho de ti y espero que estés bien. No te escribo por nada en especial. Si algún día te apetece tomar un café, me encantaría.
note: No relitigating the fight; if he replies warmly, suggest a specific day within two messages.

situation: 高校のバスケ部の顧問だった田中先生に、卒業以来10年ぶりに連絡したい。自分も今年から中学校の教員になって、部活の顧問もしている。同窓会で先生のLINEを教えてもらった。
reply: 田中先生、ご無沙汰しています。2016年卒業のバスケ部の佐藤健太です。10年ぶりのご連絡になってしまいました。実は今年の春から横浜の中学校で教員になり、女子バスケ部の顧問もしています。練習の最後に先生がいつも言っていた「最後の一本は丁寧に」を、気づけば自分も部員に言っていて、先生のことを思い出しました。先生はお変わりなくお過ごしですか。お返事はお時間のあるときで大丈夫です。
note: 空白には一文だけ触れ、具体的な思い出と近況、答えやすい問いを一つ。お願いごとは最初の連絡に入れない。

situation: I messaged my old uni friend Tom after three years of silence. He replied really warmly, said he's been meaning to reach out too, and that he's now living in Bristol, about 40 minutes from me.
reply: So good to hear from you, and Bristol is basically next door now. Want to grab lunch on Saturday 10 October? I'll come to you, and you can show me whichever pub has replaced the Crown in your affections.
note: When they reply warmly, suggest one specific day within two messages, or the momentum dies.

situation: I went quiet on my friend Leah for about 8 months during a rough patch, she texted a few times and I never replied. I'm doing better now and saw her allotment photos on Instagram. I want to reach out without a huge apology.
reply: Leah, I've been quiet for most of this year and I'm sorry I left your messages hanging; it was a rough stretch and I went to ground. I'm doing a lot better now. Those pumpkins from your allotment are ridiculous, by the way. Could I buy you a coffee soon, maybe Saturday the 10th or Sunday the 11th? No rush to reply.
note: When you were the one who went silent, one line of ownership is enough. A long apology makes her comfort you; a specific reason and a small plan move it forward.

situation: My cousin Aisha and I were really close as kids but haven't talked since our grandmother's funeral five years ago. No fight, we just drifted; she's in Manchester and I'm in Toronto. I saw on Instagram that she ran her first half marathon on Sunday.
reply: Aisha! Just saw your half marathon photos, huge congratulations. It made me think of Nani timing us racing round her garden, and how you always won. It's been far too long. How did it feel crossing the line? No rush to reply, I just wanted to say I'm proud of you.
note: Family drift gets the same shape as friends: the gap named once, one shared memory, one easy question, and no apology spiral.

situation: 林姐是我第一份工作的带教，四年没怎么联系了。她在上海，我在杭州。今天在朋友圈看到她升了市场总监，想发微信恭喜一下，但不想显得像是有事求她。
reply: 林姐，好久不见，一晃都四年了！刚看到你升了市场总监，真心替你高兴。到现在我写方案都还是先写一句话结论，这是你当年教我的。下次来杭州出差跟我说一声，我请你喝咖啡。不急着回哈。
note: 恭喜本身就是理由，不附带任何请求；一个具体的回忆比一句“恭喜恭喜”更让人记住你。

situation: My high school best friend Marco moved to Lisbon six years ago and we haven't really talked in about four. I'm in Lisbon for work from Friday Oct 16 to Monday Oct 19 and I'd love to see him. Messaging him on Instagram.
reply: Marco! It's been about four years, which is ridiculous. I'm in Lisbon for work from Friday 16 October to the Monday, and my first thought was you and all those pastel de nata photos you used to send the group chat. Any chance you're free for a coffee or a beer on the Saturday or Sunday? No pressure at all if the timing's bad.
note: A trip to their city is a natural reason to reach out: name the gap once, one shared memory, specific days, and an easy no.

situation: Ich habe meiner alten Mitbewohnerin Katrin nach drei Jahren Funkstille geschrieben. Sie hat nur kurz geantwortet: 'Hey, lange nicht gehört! Alles gut hier, und bei dir?' Ich weiß nicht, ob sie überhaupt Lust auf Kontakt hat.
reply: Bei mir alles gut, danke! Ich wohne seit März in Leipzig und arbeite jetzt in einer Buchhandlung, was mir erstaunlich gut gefällt. Machst du eigentlich noch deine Sonntagspfannkuchen? Ich denke jedes Mal an dich, wenn ich welche mache.
note: Eine kurze Antwort ist kein Nein: Länge spiegeln, ein konkretes Detail, eine leichte Frage. Antwortet sie wärmer, im nächsten Schritt ein konkretes Telefonat oder Treffen vorschlagen.

situation: 高中时我们五个女生有个微信群叫“三班五朵金花”，已经两年没人说话了。国庆我回南京待到10月6号，想在群里冒个泡，看大家有没有空聚一下。
reply: 姐妹们，这个群安静两年了，我来冒个泡。今天翻到高三运动会咱们五个穿同款红T恤的照片，笑了半天。我国庆回南京，待到6号，有谁在的话，找个下午去老门东喝杯茶？不在南京的也说说近况就好，不急着回。
note: 重启一个沉寂的群，一张具体的老照片比“好久不见”好接，邀请要具体，但不要求每个人都来。

situation: My old college friend Nate's dad died about a year ago. I saw it on Facebook at the time and never reached out, and we haven't talked since. It's been eating at me and I want to message him now.
reply: Nate, I've been meaning to write this for a long time. I saw last year that your dad had died, and I never reached out, which I regret. I'm so sorry, for your loss and for going quiet. I still think about him driving us both back to campus in that ancient Volvo, singing along to the radio. No need to reply, but if you ever fancy a beer, I'd love that.
note: Name what you missed once, briefly, then offer a real memory of the person; don't make him reassure you.

situation: 大学好友阿琪三年前突然不回我消息了，我发过几次都没回，也没吵过架，后来就断了。刚听同学说她回了厦门，还生了个女儿。我想再联系一次，但不想显得像在质问她。
reply: 阿琪，好久不见！听小敏说你回厦门了，还当了妈妈，恭喜恭喜。前几天整理东西翻到咱们大三去鼓浪屿拍的那卷胶片，你站在海边笑得眼睛都没了。宝宝叫什么名字呀？不急着回，就是想你了。
note: 先沉默的是对方时，完全不提那几年，也不问为什么；她还是不回，就不要再追。

situation: When I was 16 I did an exchange year in Lyon with the Moreau family. That was 12 years ago; we swapped Christmas cards for a while and then it stopped. I just found the photo album from that year and want to email them. Their English is good.
reply:
Dear Claire and Philippe, it's been far too long, probably ten years since my last Christmas card. I was clearing out my parents' attic this weekend and found the album from my year with you, including the photo of Julien and me covered in flour after the galette disaster. I still think of you every time I make a proper vinaigrette. How are you all, and what is Julien up to these days? No rush at all to reply, I just wanted to say hello.
With love,
Emma
note: A host family or anyone who once looked after you: name the gap once, one vivid shared memory, one easy question, no apology spiral.

situation: My friend Jas and I were inseparable in our twenties. Then I had twins three years ago and cancelled on her so often that she stopped asking; we haven't talked in over a year. The twins start preschool next week and I finally have free mornings.
reply: Jas, it's been over a year, and I know I was the one who kept cancelling, so that's on me. I walked past the Thai place on Mill Street yesterday and remembered us closing it down on your 30th. The twins start preschool next week, which means actual free mornings for the first time in three years. Could I buy you breakfast one day the week after? No pressure, and no rush to reply.
note: When your life stage caused the drift, one line of ownership, then a plan small enough that you'll actually keep it this time.

situation: 大学摄影社的学长周航比我高两届，我们只一起去拍过几次外景，毕业后八年没联系，他可能都不记得我了。我刚搬到深圳，看他朋友圈也在深圳，想跟他打个招呼。
reply: 周航学长好，不知道你还记不记得我，我是摄影社比你低两届的林悦，以前跟你们一起去拍过几次外景。一晃八年没联系了。我刚搬来深圳，看到你也在这边，就想打个招呼。你在深圳待得久，周末有什么值得去拍的地方吗？不急着回。
note: 对方可能不记得你时，第一句先帮他想起你是谁，再问一个他好回答、又能聊下去的问题。

situation: I'm Hannah. Mrs. Hughes, now 84, was our neighbour when I was a kid; she had me over after school and taught me to make scones. We moved away 15 years ago and lost touch. I'm writing her a letter by post: my mum has her address in Cardiff, I made her scone recipe last week, and I had my first baby, Ellie, in August.
reply: Dear Mrs. Hughes, It's been about fifteen years, which is far too long. I made your scones last week and could practically hear you telling me not to overwork the dough, so I wanted to write. My big news is that I had a baby girl, Ellie, in August. How are you keeping, and are you still baking? No rush at all to write back, and Mum can pass on my number if a phone call is easier. With love, Hannah
note: A paper letter to an older person can carry a little more warmth, but the shape is the same: one memory, one question, no pressure.
